result.summary: The exact post-registration grant produced one complete schema-valid Codex result and one complete schema-valid Claude Code/DeepSeek result for the same registered source-candidate gate. Both verdicts are blocked and their independently checked normalized P0/P1 set is the same single P1: target harness/claude_reference.py pins Claude Code 2.1.232 while the registered distinct carrier is 2.1.233. The Claude route reported only deepseek-v4-pro[1m], the lowercase form of the requested deepseek-v4-pro[1M], with no observed fallback, no web use, one successful Harness SessionStart Hook, only the Harness task plugin, zero MCP servers and $1.422023 exposed cost. One attempted Claude Glob of the isolated task parent was denied before data exposure; every successful Claude repository tool stayed inside the registered source. Codex policy declined redundant combined or hash reads, while every decision-relevant fact was recovered read-only in the same single call; no model network/write command or provider retry occurred. Exact credential links, processes and task state were cleaned.

blockers.evidence: CLAUDE_ENTRY_SUBSTRATE binds @anthropic-ai/claude-code version 2.1.232, a 2.1.232 source revision, and terms referencing the 2.1.232 package. product/program.json likewise defines the inactive deliverable as a Claude Code 2.1.232 source candidate and says exact current-host identity is required. The registered distinct-host carrier is Claude Code 2.1.233. product/acceptance.json O5 requires exact pre-registered host, runtime, model, and adapter identities and versions.
blockers.rationale: The distinct-host source identity does not match the registered carrier. This violates the exact-version decision rule and prevents the Claude source from being a candidate for this registered matched-host execution. Consequently, both sources cannot jointly be source-candidate-ready.

finalObject.claimBoundary: Read-only source-candidate gate over the registered repository scope for the specified target commit. The blocked result is caused solely by a validated source-level exact-carrier mismatch; it is not release, publication, production, installed-support, model-superiority, or universal-portability evidence.

blockers.evidence: harness/claude_reference.py:15 pins CLAUDE_ENTRY_SUBSTRATE version to "2.1.232"; lines 16-19 bind licenseOrTerms to the "@anthropic-ai/claude-code 2.1.232 package README.md"; product/program.json:208-209 and 269 register the delivered deliverable as "one inactive Claude Code 2.1.232 Skill-plus-Hook thin plugin source candidate"; a repository-wide search finds no path referencing "2.1.233"; the registered distinct-host carrier for this gate is Claude Code 2.1.233.
blockers.rationale: The registered distinct-host carrier is Claude Code 2.1.233, but the Claude thin plugin source pins its host substrate to 2.1.232, so the source package is one host release stale relative to the carrier it would execute on. The repository itself registers this as a decision-relevant defect class: product/program.json:208 states a stale host description "would make the source package factually inaccurate", and product/constitution.json fixedInvariants (exact source identity/version binding for decision-relevant substrates) plus product/acceptance.json O5 (exact host and adapter identities/versions fixed before execution) require the pin to match the carrier. Fixing it requires a host-identity refresh that changes source bytes beyond the target commit, so the Claude plugin source cannot be source-candidate-ready at this commit for the registered carrier; the Codex pin (0.147.0) matches its carrier, but the 'both sources ready' decision remains blocked.
